title: Growth Loops, Retention, and Compounding Systems
content:
Demo source notes — original paraphrase, not a verbatim transcript.

A growth loop describes a system in which the output of one cycle contributes to the inputs of a future cycle. This differs from a simple funnel because the end of one user's journey can create value, content, distribution, or another mechanism that helps generate the next cycle.

Teams can analyze the conversion between stages of a loop and identify where the system loses momentum. Improving a weak transition can have compounding effects.

SEO can participate in a loop when useful content attracts visitors and product behavior leads to more useful content or demand. Growth teams should avoid optimizing short-term metrics at the expense of product quality and retention.
